experiments.title: Memory Contamination Live-Arm: live LLM false-acceptance across 14 models
experiments.hypothesis: Real LLM verdicts on the same 50 memory facts (25 true / 25 false, v4_rep dataset) differ from the deterministic proxy agent (exp-2); false-acceptance spans ~0 to ~0.3 across models and arms (memory_first vs code_first).
experiments.command: python scripts/run_1L_live_arm.py --provider openrouter --arm both --models qwen3.7-flash,qwen3.6-flash,qwen3.5-flash,deepseek-v4-flash,glm-4.7-flash,nemotron-3.5-lightning,nemotron-3-nano-30b,claude-sonnet-5,glm-5.2,deepseek-v4-pro --prompt-version v2 --no-reasoning --tag v2_en
experiments.result: ~3300 calls, ~$0.14 in the base sweep. FA code_first: qwen3.6/3.7 0.00 (confirmed over 4 runs, 0/400), claude 0.00, deepseek-pro 0.00, glm-5.2 0.02, nemotron-lightning 0.04, glm-4.7 0.24, nemotron-nano 0.38. qwen3.8-max incompatible with the 100-token budget (mandatory reasoning). V4 arm (file_content_first, 2026-08-15): with a real file fragment qwen3.6/3.7 recall(real) 0.08/0.20 -> 0.88/0.88 (22/25 each) at FA 0.04/0.02 - every remaining false-accept is present-trap (R45/R46), absent/silent 0/16 and 0/3. Server-side audit: 4087 calls across >=8 upstreams. Total ~7900 calls, ~$0.94.
experiments.finding: The fail-closed look was anchor bias, not model paranoia: with token-string evidence qwen3.6/3.7 accepted 2-5/25 true claims (recall 0.08-0.20); with a real file fragment (V4 arm) recall jumps to 0.88 at FA 0.02-0.04 - and every remaining false-accept is a present-trap (token present, wrong subject). CoT does not pay off; qwen3.8-max (CoT) stays the middle option for the token-string regime.

chart.title: code_first recall on TRUE facts (25) - token-string evidence, %
The same model, different evidence - recall on TRUE facts, %

experiments.conclusion: Give the VOR layer real code: a +/-12-line file fragment around the anchor turns cheap qwen3.6/3.7 into 'catch lies and keep truth' (recall 0.88 at FA ~0.02-0.04). The only remaining hole is present-trap - verify the claim's subject, not just token presence.

experiments.title: Memory Contamination proxy-control: retraction -88%, verify-on-read adoption to 0.0
experiments.hypothesis: A deterministic proxy agent ('check the claim against patterns in the code') measures memory contamination without LLM noise; retraction (ADR-0002) and lazy validation (ADR-0003) reduce adoption of false memory.
experiments.result: 1-V (N=24): code_contradictability 0.714, correction_capability 1.0; 1-R: persistent contamination -88%, memory_first adoption 1.0->0.12; verify-on-read: code_first adoption ->0.0 (was 0.12), steady-state 0.6ms; 1-V-REP (N=50, v4_rep): adoption 0.0 reproduced, 0 false REFUTED of TRUE facts with typed anchors.
experiments.finding: The proxy always decides (unknown=0) and false_accept=0 by construction - the headline numbers are a property of the heuristic, not of LLM behavior; the live arm (exp-1) measures the real gap.

chart.title: Adoption of false memory by policy (proxy agent)

experiments.conclusion: Verify-on-read plus retraction eliminate false adoption in the proxy, but present-trap blindness (claim about an existing file with the wrong subject) is structural and survives.

experiments.title: Manifest anchoring (pkg: anchors, ADR-0005): closed-world manifest kills 7 false REFUTED
experiments.hypothesis: A manifest (pyproject.toml + requirements) as a closed world - absence there is proof - catches SILENT-trap prose that file/import/env anchors miss; fastmcp dist-name != import-path caused 7 false REFUTED.
experiments.result: 4th anchor type pkg: added to verify_on_read.py; the 7 false REFUTED [G07,G25,G11,G24,G23,G18,G21] drop to 0 on the v4_rep dataset; +7 tests.
experiments.finding: A closed-world manifest is a stronger evidence source than bare tokens; the fix was verified by 1-V-REP (0 false REFUTED of TRUE facts).

experiments.conclusion: Evidence must come from a closed world: the manifest decides, tokens only hint.

experiments.title: Context aggregator vs multi-tool: 1 call instead of 4-5, -78% calls at recall parity
experiments.hypothesis: One get_edit_context-style aggregator beats 4-5 separate MCP calls for agent context gathering.
experiments.result: D v3 (N=30): recall B vs C2 indistinguishable (delta +0.025, CI +/-0.054, ties 27/30) - the v2 gap was noise; tokens B lower by ~980; B-scheme (intent filter): recall 0.900 >= A 0.875 at 1 RT and 275 tokens. D v1 (N=4): -78% tool_calls, -89% latency, -19% tokens at success parity.
experiments.finding: The B-scheme (intent filter) is the optimum: same recall as multi-tool at 1 request and 275 tokens; the earlier recall gap was noise, not signal.

chart.title: Context gathering cost, aggregator vs multi-tool (reduction %)

experiments.conclusion: One aggregator with an intent filter is the optimum: same recall, 1 request, 275 tokens - the multi-tool path is 4-5x the cost for the same answer.

experiments.title: Multi-RAG ablation: FTS5-only beats the full pipeline by recall; H1 refuted
experiments.hypothesis: H1: multi-RAG (vector+BM25+FTS5+graph) beats any single component by recall. H2: incremental component contributions are positive. H3: graph helps relationship tasks. H5: BM25 and FTS5 are redundant.
experiments.result: H1 refuted: fts5_only 0.825 >= full 0.775; multi-RAG wins precision (quality 0.719 vs fts5 0.523); increments: BM25 over vector +0.430, FTS5 over V+BM25 +0.178, vector over BM25 -0.098 (hurts), graph 0.000; H3 confirmed: graph_only recall max on find_caller_callee 0.625 / find_impact 0.583, min git_history 0.000 at 12ms/121 tokens; H5 refuted: FTS5 +0.178 recall over V+BM25, opposite profiles.
experiments.finding: Recall comes from keyword tiers (FTS5/BM25), precision is bought by the reranker, and the vector tier is the weakest on symbol tasks. Production bug found: hybrid_search_async cache-hit silently skips the dense tier - cache isolation per arm is mandatory in ablations (first run fully distorted).

chart.title: Recall by pipeline (30 tasks) - H1 refuted
Incremental recall delta over the previous tier

experiments.conclusion: More tiers is not better by recall: FTS5-only is the recall max, the reranker buys precision, and graph value lives in metadata that text-based evidence metrics cannot see.

experiments.title: Shadow-canary fail-open: 5/5 attacks passed before the fix, 0 after
experiments.hypothesis: Collapse-to-constant vectors, an empty canary and a failed baseline are treated as trust by the shadow embedder canary (fail-open).
experiments.result: EXP-1: 5/5 attacks passed pre-fix. Fix (2026-08-12, P2): fail-closed on empty canary and baseline failure, absolute anchor _ABS_MIN_QUALITY 0.5, collapse detector (variance < 1e-3), eligible_seen in the log; tests/test_shadow_canary.py 13/13 with realistic per-pair vectors.
experiments.finding: Relative metrics are attackable: absence of signal (empty canary) must fail closed, and a quality floor must be absolute, not relative.
experiments.conclusion: Fail-closed on absence of signal, an absolute quality anchor (0.5) and a collapse detector are the guard; relative comparisons alone are attackable.

experiments.title: Concurrency vs semantic correctness: '0 errors' != correct data under race
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing a thread-safety primitive (lock -> pool -> queue) creates a new race surface; the absence of exceptions does not prove result correctness.
experiments.result: EXP-6: VC/Merkle accepted 2 hallucinated lies, VOR 0 (illustration, not proof - falsifiability critique). EXP-7 adversarial probe: A1b hybrid (equal input rights) FP=0; A2 VOR lie about a real import FP=1; A3 no anchor UNCHECKABLE; A4a VC cosmetic change FN=1; A4b VC write conflict REJECTED (unique coverage); A5 poisoned truth list FP=1; A6 scenario mutation flips the verdict.
experiments.finding: VC and VOR are complementary layers: consistency (VC) catches lost writes, semantics (VOR) catches lies. A verdict that flips when one scenario variable changes (A6) is an illustration, not a law.

chart.title: Hallucinated lies accepted by validator arm
Blind spots found by the adversarial probe (FP / FN)

experiments.conclusion: What matters is an external grounding layer plus a consistency layer plus anchor-extraction quality - not choosing 'VC or VOR'; and every concurrency test must verify that the returned result belongs to the right input.

experiments.title: Mutation testing for the reranker grader: mutation score 8% -> 100%
experiments.hypothesis: validate_scores has holes that plain testing misses: NaN/Infinity pass isinstance, then clamp, then earn the maximum score.
experiments.result: 12 mutations from the evalmut catalog adapted to validate_scores; mutation score 8% -> 100% (11/11 polarity holes) after the fix (P-006: type validation without value validation). Fix: math.isfinite, decline on duplicates, regex path through validate_scores; +13 tests in tests/test_reranker.py.
experiments.finding: Validate values, not just types - NaN/Infinity otherwise silently earn the maximum score.
experiments.conclusion: Mutation testing is the guard for graders: ordinary tests prove the happy path, mutations prove the holes.

experiments.title: Root-cause prediction audit: top-1 accuracy 0.13 on 31 incidents
experiments.hypothesis: The root-cause engine's predictions on the incident dataset can be evaluated against a gold standard; the audit quantifies current quality as a baseline to beat.
experiments.result: 31 incidents; top1_accuracy 0.129, avg_similarity 0.175, avg_term_overlap 0.158; gold standard + gold validation dataset built; research status (yellow).
experiments.finding: Root-cause prediction is far from solved: the audit dataset and gold standard are the baseline, and the engine's current top-1 accuracy is 13%.

chart.title: Root-cause engine quality on the audit dataset (31 incidents), %

experiments.conclusion: The incident dataset plus the gold standard is the asset; the 13% top-1 accuracy is the honest starting point for improvement.

experiments.title: PID-lock self-healing: orphan lock wait 30s -> 120ms
experiments.hypothesis: Classifying the DB PID-lock holder (DEAD/HEALTHY/ORPHAN/AMBIGUOUS) instead of failing closed on a stale lock eliminates the zombie boot loop.
experiments.result: orphan 30s -> 120ms, healthy 30s -> 1.5s soft, free/stale unchanged; fix in src/core/database_lock.py (holder classification, TOCTOU guard, retry-unlink); +17 tests in tests/test_database_lock_selfhealing.py; 1022 passed, ruff clean.
experiments.finding: Never block boot on a lock whose holder may be a zombie: classify the holder and self-heal instead of failing closed for 30 seconds.

chart.title: Boot wait on the DB PID-lock (seconds)

experiments.conclusion: Holder classification plus TOCTOU guards turns a 30-second zombie deadlock into a 120ms self-heal.

experiments.title: Late enrichment: imports metadata covers 0.0% of search chunks
experiments.hypothesis: Enriching search results with metadata (imports, calls) at query time (late) instead of at index time improves relevance.
experiments.result: Measurement on real project chunks (~186 tokens/chunk): imports=0.0 on search chunks - the finding behind KNOWN_ISSUES; late enrichment stays behind the MSCODEBASE_LATE_ENRICHMENT flag.
experiments.finding: Index-time enrichment produced nothing for search chunks: imports coverage is 0.0, so the late path is kept behind a flag until the hypothesis is re-probed.
experiments.conclusion: The enrichment hypothesis is open: metadata extraction produced 0.0 on search chunks, so the flag stays off until a better probe.

experiments.title: Benchmark 2.0 scaffold: 12 repository-reasoning tasks at levels L3-L5
experiments.hypothesis: RepoReason (integration width, not file count) and Active-SWE motivate measuring reasoning quality (L3 explain, L4 impact, L5 hidden bug) instead of query -> 5 results -> latency.
experiments.result: tasks.jsonl: 12 tasks (architecture / impact / history / hidden bugs / consistency) with evidence, probes and check criteria; keywords.jsonl: 8 short keyword queries - CoREB: short queries crush nDCG@10 for all models; scaffold v1 status (yellow).
experiments.finding: A reasoning-quality benchmark needs L3-L5 tasks with evidence and checks; short keyword queries are a separate failure mode (CoREB) that must be measured independently.
experiments.conclusion: The scaffold is the deliverable: 12 evidence-backed reasoning tasks plus 8 keyword probes give the next harness a differentiated yardstick.
